CAV JUDGMENT (PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY)
1. RULE. Learned APP waives service of rule for the respondent-State.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 2.

The present appeal has been preferred by the appellant under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 challenging the judgment and order dated 30.06.2014 passed by Sessions Judge,
Valsad in Sessions Case No.70 of 2009, whereby the appellant herein has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) read with Section 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (herein after referred to as the "IPC") and is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, further simple imprisonment of 3 (Three) months is imposed.
3.
The facts and circumstances giving rise to the filing of present appeal are such that on 14.08.2004, it was the festival of Janmashtmi.
On that day, the prosecutrix after offering her prayers at Ramji Temple was going for tuition on her Hero Honda Pleasure 2 wheeler bearing Registration No.GJ-15-TC-59.
When she reached at the place of incident, two persons came from the opposite direction on the Pulsar Motorcycle.

After traveling some distance in the direction opposite to the direction in which the prosecutrix was going, two persons, who were riding on Pulsar Motorcycle started following her and they came near the vehicle of the prosecutrix and one of the accused kicked the vehicle on which the prosecutrix was riding.
Due to the said kick, the prosecutrix fell down on the road.
From there, she was dragged by these two persons to the bushes.
They forcibly removed her clothes and one by one committed a rape on her.
Thereafter, they threatened the prosecutrix that if she informed about the incident to anybody, they will kill her.
The prosecutrix raised some shouts.
Out of two persons, one person asked the other to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined get the motorcycle, and thereafter, both of them ran away.
The prosecutrix was thereafter waiting on the road for help.
The person viz. Sanjaybhai Budhabhai, who was going towards Village:Dungari saw her sitting there.
The prosecutrix from the mobilephone of the said Sanjaybhai Budhabhai, informed her father on telephone about the incident.
The prosecutrix had sustained injuries on the various parts of her body.
The prosecutrix herself lodged the FIR with regard to the said incident with Dungari Police Station.
Pursuant to the same, FIR being I.C.R.No.41 of 2009 came to be registered against unknown accused persons.

Thereafter, the investigation into the offence was carried out and the present appellant and another co-accused were found to be involved in the offence in question and since there was sufficient material available against the them, the Investigating Agency had filed Faruk Said Lambat vs State Of Gujarat on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402942/
2 charge-sheet against both the accused persn for the relevant offences.
4. Since the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) alleged against the accused persons was exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions, the Magistrate committed the proceedings to the Court of Sessions under Section 209 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereupon, the Sessions Judge framed charges against the appellant and another convict vide Exh.8 for the relevant offences more particularly, offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) read with Section 114 of the IPC.
Thereafter, the Sessions Court had recorded the plea of both the convicts and since both of them pleaded not guilty, they were put to trial.
The prosecution had examined as many as 26 witnesses and had also produced several documents on record to bring home the charge against the accused persons.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 5.

The Sessions Court, after considering the evidence adduced on record and after hearing both the sides, was pleased to convict both the accused for the relevant offence including offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) read with Section 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

The convict - Munaf was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for 10 years and fine of Rs.10,000/-, whereas appellant herein has been convicted for the same offence and is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, further simple imprisonment of 3 (Three) months is imposed vide judgent and order dated 30.06.2014.
6. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the same, the appellant has preferred present appeal.
7. At this stage, it is stated at bar that the convict - Munaf @ Lalo Ibrahim Ahmed Shaikh has not filed any appeal against the impugned judgment and order.
It is also stated at bar that he has already undergone the sentence imposed upon him.
8. Learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that the Sessions Court while convicting the appellant for the offence in question has heavily relied upon the deposition of the prosecutrix.

In view of the fact that the prosecution has not examined the Tuition Teacher and the other Students,
who are attending the tuition along with prosecutrix.
the deposition of the prosecutrix does not appear to be reliable.

8.1 Learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that the Test Identification Parade has not been carried out in a legal NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED:
20/07/2023 undefined manner, and therefore, the identification of the present appellant by the prosecutrix in Test Identification Parade is doubtful.
8.2
Learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that the history given by the appellant before the Doctor is inadmissible in evidence in view of provision of Section 26 of the Evidence Act.

The prosecution story that the appellant kicked the two wheeler of the prosecutrix from his two wheeler is not acceptable as though the prosecutrix fell down on the road as per the prosecution, she had not sustained any corresponding injuries.

In the alternative, he submitted that for the same set of Faruk Said Lambat vs State Of Gujarat on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402942/
3 evidence, the Sessions Court has imposed sentence of 10 years upon another convict-Munaf,
whereas for the very same set of evidence, sentence of life imprisonment is imposed against the present appellant.

entities.text: Faruk Said Lambat vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are no special circumstances available on record which would warrant imposition of more stringent punishment upon the appellant.
He, therefore, submitted to allow the present appeal by appropriately quashing and setting aside the impugned judgment and order.
9. Learned APP has opposed the appeal, inter alia, contending that the prosecutrix in her deposition has clearly narrated the manner in which the incident had taken place.
There is no reason available on record to disbelieve the deposition of the prosecutrix.
The version of the prosecutrix also finds support and corroboration from other material available on record.
She, therefore, submitted that the Sessions Court has not committed any error in convicting the present appellant for the relevant offences and imposing sentence of life imprisonment upon him.
She, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 10.
Heard learned advocates appearing for both the parties and perused the material on record.
Since it is the case of offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) of the IPC, the deposition of the prosecutrix attains significance.
The prosecutrix in her deposition vide Exh.33 has clearly stated that the incident had taken place on 14.08.2009.
She was aged about 16 years at the relevant time.
It was the festival of Janmashtmi on that day.
At around 5.45 in the morning, she was going to Ramji Temple for offering her prayers on her Hero Honda Pleasure two wheeler.
When she reached the outskirts of Village:Dhanoli, 2 persons came from the opposite direction on a Pulsar Motorcycle and crossed the prosecutrix.
After going for some distance, these two persons took "U" turn and started following her.
Near the outskirts of Village:Kota, these two persons kicked the two wheeler of the prosecutrix, and therefore, her vehicle had turned turtle.
Thereafter, she was dragged to nearby bushes by those two persons and they had forcibly removed her clothes, and thereafter, one by one committed a rape on her.
Thereafter, both the persons ran away towards the direction of Village:Dhanoli.
Those two persons had also taken a key of her two wheeler and a mobilephone of Nokia Company with them and had also threatened of killing her, if she informed anybody about the incident.
She, thereafter, informed her father on telephone about the incident and lodged FIR with the Dungari Police Station.
The witness has been cross-examined in detail in defense of the appellant.
Upon perusal of entire cross-examination, it appears that the version given by the prosecutrix in her examination-in- chief has remained unchallenged.
It is sought to be contended on behalf of the appellant that as per the case of prosecution, the prosecutrix was going for her tuition at the time of incident.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined
However, the prosecution has not examined the tuition teacher and other co-students of the prosecutrix.
Therefore, the theory of the prosecution case is not believable.
Merely because the prosecution has not examined the aforesaid witnesses, what is stated by the prosecutrix in her deposition does not become unreliable.
What is required to be proved by the prosecution is an incident of rape and not the fact that the prosecutrix was going for tuition.

Assuming for the sake of argument that the prosecutrix was not going for tuition at the time of incident that by itself does not Faruk Said Lambat vs State Of Gujarat on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402942/
4 make the case of prosecution unreliable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. The deposition of the prosecutrix also finds support from the fact that after their arrest, both the convicts were subjected to Test Identification Parade, wherein the prosecutrix had successfully identified both the convicts.
An objection is sought to be raised against the conduct of Test Identification Parade for the sake of it.
Learned advocate for the appellant has failed to demonstrate as to how the conduct of Test Identification Parade was not proper.
The prosecution has duly proved the conduct of Test Identification Parade by examining the P.W.17 Kishorbhai Anandshankar Pandya, Executive Magistrate & Mamlatdar vide Exh.71.

This witness in his deposition narrates the procedure undertaken by him for conduct of Test Identification Parade and there appears no irregularity or illegality in conduct of the said Test Identification Parade.
12. The medical evidence in this regard also attains significance.
The prosecution has examined P.W.9 Dr.Dineshprasad Jagoprasad Mandal vide Exh.49.
He is the Doctor, who had examined the prosecutrix after the incident.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined
This witness, in his deposition, enumerates the external injuries found on the body of the prosecutrix.
He further states that hymen of the prosecutrix was broken.
There were signs of sexual violence on the body of the prosecutrix and the possibility of the penetration and rape could not be ruled out.
The witness had also taken vaginal swab, blood, Nail, Saliva and pubic hair from the body of the prosecutrix as samples.
This witness has also been cross
- examined by learned counsel appearing for the defence and nothing contrary to what is stated by the witness in his examination-in-chief emanates from the cross-examination.
This aspect also supports the version of the prosecturix.
13. The samples collected by Dr.Dineshprasad Mandal during the medical examination of the prosecutrix were sent to the FSL.
The other material including a piece of underwear worn by the prosecutrix at the time of incident was also sent to FSL along with DNA samples of both the convicts.
14. The prosecution has also examined witness P.W.10 Meenaben Rajnikant Dave vide Exh.55.
She is the witness, who had conducted DNA Test of the aforesaid articles at the FSL.

In her deposition,
she has clearly stated that the DNA of sperm found present on the piece of underwear worn by the prosecutrix at the time of incident and her vaginal swab matches with the DNA of both the convicts.
This piece of evidence completely nails both the convicts for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) of the IPC.
15.

For the foregoing reasons, the Sessions Court does not appear to have committed any error in convicting the present appellant for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT
DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined the IPC.
16. The second limb of arguments of learned advocate appearing for the appellant is with regard to the sentence imposed upon the appellant.

It is an admitted position emerging from the record that the present appellant and the co-convict Munaf were accompanying each other at the time of Faruk Said Lambat vs State Of Gujarat on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402942/
5 incident and they both had committed rape on the prosecutrix one by one.

entities.text: Faruk Said Lambat vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Still, the Sessions Court has imposed sentence of imprisonment for 10 years upon Munaf, whereas the appellant has been sentenced to undergo life imprisonment.
17. From the record, it appears that, in the opinion of the Sessions Court, the act was premeditated by the present appellant.
The Sessions Court has also observed that there appears no circumstances of any remorse or improvement in the conduct of the present appellant.

So far the aspect of premeditation is concerned, there is nothing on record nor it is the case of prosecution that the present appellant knew the prosecutrix and that he was also aware that the prosecutrix was going for tuition all alone.
As per the case of prosecution itself, co-incidentally the prosecutrix and the present appellant crossed each other, and thereafter, the appellant had started following her.
Thus, the aspect of any premeditation on the part of the appellant is ruled out.

It appears that the history given by the co-convict Munaf before the Doctor at the time of his medical examination appears to have weighed with the Sessions court for coming to the aforesaid conclusion.

When the co-convict Munaf gave history before the Doctor, he was in police custody, and therefore, in view of the provision of Section 26 of the Evidence NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined Act, the said history was not admissible in evidence.

entities.text: Evidence NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2014 CAV JUDGMENT
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 18. So far as the aspect of remorse or improvement qua the appellant is concerned, there is nothing on record to indicate that the appellant showed signs of no remorse or that he was not likely to improve.
As per the settled legal position, the cogent reasons are required to be given for imposing stringent and strict sentence.

The reasons given by the Sessions Court for imposing life imprisonment against the appellant do not inspire any confidence more particularly, when the co-convict Munaf has been imposed sentence of imprisonment for 10 years relying upon the very set of evidence as against the present appellant.
The jail record indicates that the present appellant has undergone sentence of more than 12 years and 5 months.

The sentence undergone by the appellant,
in the opinion of this Court, is sufficient for the offence for which the appellant is convicted.
19. Under the circumstances, the present appeal is partly allowed to the aforesaid extent.
The appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
R & P be sent back to the concerned Trial Court, forthwith.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
